label: def:antiderivative
title: Antiderivative
statement: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. A function $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is an \emph{antiderivative} of $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ on the open interval $\mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b = (a,b)$ if for every $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$, $F$ has derivative $f(x)$ at $x$ (in the sense of \texttt{HasDerivAt}). In the Lean formalization this is \texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn F f a b}, defined as $\forall x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b,\; \texttt{HasDerivAt}\; F\; (f\; x)\; x$. Note that $a$ and $b$ need not satisfy $a < b$; when $a \ge b$ the interval is empty and the condition is vacuously true.
